transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-23
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Ellis (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Neill (PolarisPrint Head of AI Ops), Sofia Martinez (Infra Lead), Priya Anand (Procurement), Noah Kim (Platform Eng)

Summary:
PolarisPrint is evaluating a 12-month contract extension with a capacity uplift and activation of EU and APAC regions (staged). Key asks: predictable burst credits, lower p99 latency for EU customers, SOC2 paperwork and KMS integration for key management. SE-led benchmarking to validate latency targets; procurement needs updated quote and terms.

Topics: capacity uplift, multi-region activation (EU, APAC), contract extension term and pricing, private VPC onramp, SOC2/KMS/SSO questions, bench methodology

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call - we'll keep this short, 45 to 60 ish minutes. Today's to align on the PolarisPrint renewal ask and the region bump, and agree next steps. Liam, Sofia - you there?
[00:12] Liam: Yep, here. Thanks Maya. Appreciate keeping it tight.
[00:15] Sofia: Hi all.
[00:17] Priya: Hi, Priya here.
[00:19] Noah: Noah on the line.
[00:21] Maya: Great. Quick overview - you told us in the doc last week you're looking to up committed capacity by roughly 2.5x and spin up EU + APAC for year-end customers, plus a 12-month extension instead of month-to-month. We wanted to confirm the mix (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and the timing. Ravi, want to cover bench plan?
[00:37] Ravi: Sure. We'll run two passes - steady state and burst window. Steady state simulates 450 rps per region, burst will be a 10 minute 2k rps test to validate autoscale and our burst credits. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail latency and token cost. Note: our staging infra is a clone of your config but uses Redwood Dedi pools - might be slightly different from prod if you use on-prem.
[00:58] Liam: That burst number sounds reasonable. Main thing is we need p99 under 300ms for EU use cases, otherwise we have to keep logic server-side. How confident are you on p99 with the quantized 13B models we run?
[01:16] Ravi: With continuous batching and the latest kernel picks, our internal tests on 13B-quant show p99 around 220ms for 2k token seqs on nVidia A40 equivalent. But two caveats: your seq lengths and KV cache perf matter, and if you go private on prem with different NICs we may see variance. We'll surface raw traces.
[01:38] Sofia: When you say "kernel picks" is that automatic? We need to know if we'll be forced to change quantization or model variants.
[01:46] Ravi: It's automatic in the runtime - we pick kernels and quant profiles per model and sequence distribution. For your workload we'll recommend a medium quant profile to keep accuracy and tail latency. We'll call that out in the bench report.
[02:00] Liam: Okay. On the commercial side Priya and I need the uptick pricing and burst credits spelled out. Also wondering if there's a discount for committing to 12 months vs 6.
[02:12] Maya: Yes. We'll send an updated quote with tiered pricing - 12-month term includes a 12% commit discount and two burst credits per month (each credit covers a 10-minute 2k burst). If you want more burst credits, we can show a per-credit price.
[02:28] Priya: Good. Also please include egress and data residency fees for EU. Last time those weren't explicit.
[02:35] Maya: Will do.
[02:36] Noah: Quick technical Q - for the VPC private onramp, we need KMS integration — our security team requires keys to be in our Azure Key Vault and we want to confirm HSM-backed options.
[02:49] Jordan (CSM): We've done Azure KMS integrations with a few customers; Redwood Private supports passing through to your KMS. HSM support is via the customer-provided HSM or partner HSM — we'll attach the integration guide.
[03:03] Sofia: And SOC2/ISO paperwork? Our compliance folks will want the full pack and a point of contact for auditors.
[03:10] Maya: We'll share the security binder and SOC2 report redacted, plus the auditor contact list for last cycle. I'll include our SSO/SAML docs — some places see the SAML assertion config as SAML2 so you may see variations in docs.
[03:23] Liam: Great. Also, can you clarify audit log retention? We may need 13 months.
[03:29] Jordan: Default is 90 days for hosted, but for Dedicated and Private we can extend retention as an add-on. We'll include options.
[03:36] Sofia: Network-wise, we have asymmetrical routing and a 50MB/s egress cap per region during peak; will that impact your burst tests? We can temporarily lift for the test but need to schedule.
[03:49] Ravi: Important to know. If egress is 50MB/s that could hit before CPU/GPU limits depending on payload sizes. For the short burst test we recommend temporarily increasing to 500MB/s for the test window. We'll need a test start time preferably off-peak.
[04:03] Liam: We can do 02:00 UTC next Tuesday? Priya, is that okay for procurement?
[04:08] Priya: Yes, that's fine for the pilot window. We'll need an internal change request though.
[04:12] Maya: Noted.
[04:14] [05:00] Speaker 1: (background) mhm
[04:20] Ravi: On fallback policies — if EU capacity is saturated we can route requests to a compatible variant in US with a slightly higher latency and lower cost. We also have automatic model variant fallback that uses a 7B variant if 13B is unavailable; cost/capacity trade offs shown in the console.
[04:38] Sofia: Fallback to US is okay as long as we meet data residency controls for EU customers. Is routing logged and auditable?
[04:46] Jordan: Yes, all routing decisions are in the request trace; we can add a tag for residency-sensitive requests.
[04:53] Liam: Competitor question: EdgeServe told us they can do EU on-prem in two weeks. How fast can Redwood spin up a private node?
[05:01] Maya: For Private on-prem it's usually 6-8 weeks for initial staging with our playbook (network, install, KMS, certs). For VPC-hosted private it's 3-4 weeks. EdgeServe's two weeks claim is ambitious; often it misses KMS/certs and audit prep.
[05:18] Priya: Good context for procurement.
[05:20] Noah: Any changes to observability? We need token-level cost per request broken down to model and route in your console.
[05:28] Jordan: That's exactly in the new console view - token cost per model, per route, plus anomaly alerts tied to eval prompts. We can enable a 90-day retention or longer for enterprise.
[05:39] Ravi: For the benchmark we'll push per-token tracing and include a cost delta analysis between 13B and the 7B fallbacks.
[05:48] Liam: Great. One more on SLAs - what's the p99 SLA we can get for Dedicated in EU?
[05:54] Maya: Our Dedicated SLA covers availability, with latency SLOs per model class, but p99 latency SLAs are offered as part of an enterprise addendum. We'll flag that in the quote.
[06:06] Sofia: Onboarding timeline if we sign by June 10? We want EU region live by end of July.
[06:13] Maya: For Hosted EU activation it's 4 weeks from signed SOW; Dedicated pools and private onramp extend that timeline. If you sign by June 10, Hosted EU live by mid-July is realistic; Dedicated by end-of-July if we prioritize provisioning.
[06:27] Liam: Sounds ok.
[06:29] [20:00] Ravi: (reads) Bench methodology recap - we'll run: 1) steady state 45 min at regional target rps with seq dist similar to your traffic, 2) two 10 minute burst windows, 3) a sustained 1hr soak at 50% uplift. We'll collect pod-level metrics, gpu utilization, kv miss rates.
[06:48] Sofia: About KV miss rates - we use a lot of prefix caching for customer prompts. How does Redwood's KV cache persist across autoscale events?
[06:56] Ravi: The runtime keeps KV cache in local memory and does a handoff on scale-downs to ensure warm starts where possible, but there can be cold starts. We recommend prefix caching in your application layer where possible. We'll include warm-start metrics in the bench.
[07:11] Liam: Ok. Any risk to output quality with the medium quant profile you recommended? We run sensitive summarization jobs.
[07:18] Ravi: Medium quant usually has negligible quality delta for summarization tasks; we'll run a small eval set during bench to quantify regressions and include delta numbers.
[07:27] Priya: For procurement: please include a clause for termination if regional latency SLA not met for two consecutive months.
[07:33] Maya: We can propose a credit scheme rather than termination; we'll draft options.
[07:38] Liam: That works.
[07:40] [35:00] Maya: Let's recap next steps so procurement has clarity: we'll send the 12-month extension quote with line items for EU and APAC region activation, burst credits, optional extended log retention, and Dedicated SLA addendum. SE will schedule the bench next Tuesday 02:00 UTC pending your egress lift. Jordan will attach SOC2 and KMS integration guides and the list of references.
[07:58] Priya: Can you also surface references that used EU onramp in the last 6 months? That helps procurement.
[08:04] Jordan: We'll include two references - one retail and one fintech (redacted).
[08:08] Noah: Any blockers from our side? We'll get network diagram and egress ticket in by Friday.
[08:14] Sofia: I'll upload network diagram and the egress change form by Friday EOD.
[08:19] Maya: Perfect. Anything else?
[08:21] Liam: No, that's it. Thanks all.
[08:23] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the quote and bench schedule.

Action items (quick list):
- Ravi to run benchmarks and deliver raw traces + bench report (due 2026-06-02)
- Maya to share contract draft, pricing and SLA addendum (due 2026-05-27)
- Jordan to send SOC2 pack, SSO/SAML and KMS integration docs & references (due 2026-05-25)
- Sofia to provide network diagram and egress change request (due 2026-05-28)

Links referenced: "renewal playbook" (internal deck), staging bench spreadsheet (will be shared via link), SOC2 binder (attached in follow-up email).

End of transcript.
